GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
Worldline has reached the point where browser failures should become inspectable through product contracts instead of requiring knowledge of CEF internals, provider stdout or bespoke test fixtures. The next shell will need a diagnostic surface, later agents may need narrowly authorized observations, and support/debug workflows need a stable vocabulary that survives browser provider replacement.
The design deliberately separates three things that conventional Chromium tooling often combines: engine fact extraction, Worldline diagnostic state, and a developer UI. CEF may know how a console message or resource event is emitted. The `worldline-browser-devtools` service owns the normalized bounded diagnostic view. A future shell plugin decides how to render it. None of those responsibilities belongs in the kernel.
The intended topology is therefore conceptually:
browser engine callback / provider fact -> engine-neutral diagnostic DTO -> bounded browser diagnostics service -> authorized query / optional metadata notification -> shell, support tool or agent consumer
A native CEF DevTools window can still be useful when a human operator needs deep engine-specific inspection. It is treated as an optional privileged escape hatch rather than as the Worldline API, because its semantics and authority are much broader than ordinary diagnostic observation.

Alternatives.Alternative: Embed Chrome/CEF DevTools as the canonical Worldline diagnostics feature. This is not selected because it couples product contracts and future shell behavior to Chromium, makes second-engine support expensive, and exposes a large mutation surface when many consumers only need observation.

Expose raw Chrome DevTools Protocol through a generic method/json passthrough. This is not selected for v0.1 because it leaks Chromium vocabulary across the provider boundary, makes authority nearly all-or-nothing, and creates a difficult security and compatibility contract before Worldline has evidence that such power is required.

Enable a remote debugging port and let tools connect directly to Chromium. This is not selected because it creates a separate network-facing control plane, bypasses normal Worldline capability admission, and is unnecessary for the bounded diagnostic proving slice.

Publish every console and network record directly onto the generic event bus. This is not selected because page diagnostics are potentially high-volume and sensitive. A bounded service-owned buffer with explicit queries provides clearer retention, overflow and authority semantics. Metadata-only update events may still be useful later without making the event bus the data store.

Store diagnostics durably from the first version so users can inspect old sessions after restart. This is not selected because console text and full URLs can contain sensitive information and because a durable recorder needs its own retention, deletion, redaction and data-ownership policy. The first slice should measure usefulness and volume with bounded ephemeral state.

Put browser diagnostic buffers in the kernel so every provider gets them for free. This is not selected because diagnostic entries are browser-domain entities and nothing about their semantics is required for generic plugin lifecycle, authority or transport enforcement.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: The approved plan must inspect the pinned CEF 151 binding and identify the maintained callbacks or provider mechanisms for console and resource/network facts, including callback thread affinity and object lifetime. The spec does not assume a particular CEF callback name where repository evidence has not yet established it.

The plan will choose the smallest engine-side seam. A separately versioned experimental `browser.engine.diagnostics/0.1` primitive is acceptable if a provider-facing trait is insufficient, but the public service remains `browser.devtools/0.1` and no CEF/CDP object crosses it.

The plan will select concrete per-page/per-context entry counts, aggregate byte budgets, maximum message/URL/source lengths and cursor page sizes from a bounded test workload. Those numbers become measured plan/ADR parameters, not hidden implementation defaults.

The exact network record shape depends on what the real provider can report reliably without response-body/header capture or raw CDP. HTTP status, MIME, transfer size and timing fields may be optional and presence-qualified rather than fabricated when unavailable.

Console source URLs and network URLs may need different normalization or display projections. Full values remain available only inside the admitted diagnostic scope; generic metrics and update events should carry counts, categories or opaque IDs instead of sensitive query strings.

The plan will decide whether a diagnostic buffer starts a fresh logical segment on every DocumentRevision or retains a bounded tail of older revisions. In either case every record must retain explicit document identity and queries must not present old records as current-page facts.

The optional provider-native DevTools window remains deliberately separable. If the pinned CEF provider exposes a safe local show/open operation that can be automated without remote debugging exposure, the plan may include it with a stronger authority. If proving it expands the security scope materially, it remains deferred without blocking the normalized diagnostics service.

The plan will determine whether diagnostic update notifications add enough UI value to justify an ephemeral metadata event. Raw console/network payloads do not need to be copied to the generic event bus simply to make a future panel feel live.

The S3D fixture should reuse deterministic loopback infrastructure where possible but remain a separately named proving slice. It must exercise the service through the normal native provider path rather than by injecting normalized records directly as the sole production evidence.

Scenarios.Scenario: A loopback page logs one normal marker, one warning and one error. An authorized diagnostic consumer for that PageId reads all three through the Worldline service with document identity and bounded source/location data.

The same page loads one successful resource and one deterministic 404 or failed resource. The diagnostic network view reports their distinct outcomes without exposing cookies, authorization headers, bodies or response content.
Two BrowserContexts load the same loopback URL. A principal authorized only for Context A cannot read console or network entries from Context B even if it knows B's PageId or an entry identifier.

A fixture emits thousands of console records. The service reaches a declared bound, drops/truncates according to policy, increments visible overflow metadata and leaves navigation and rendering usable instead of growing memory without limit.

A page navigates to a new document. Old diagnostic entries remain explicitly tagged with the prior DocumentRevision or are discarded according to the chosen bounded policy; they are never silently attributed to the new page content.

The diagnostics service crashes or is unloaded while browsing continues. The page, request-policy plugin, downloads, cookies, tabs and history continue to operate; after restart the diagnostics runtime has fresh authority and no stale cursor/handle from the previous RuntimeId is accepted.
An agent or plugin with ordinary page observation authority attempts to read raw console text. Access is denied until a separately admitted diagnostic observation grant is present.

A trusted local operator requests provider-native DevTools. If the provider advertises that optional capability and the caller has its stronger grant, Worldline may open the native tool locally. Unsupported providers fail explicitly; ordinary diagnostic readers never receive a raw CEF handle or remote-debugging endpoint.

The real hosted S3D run records provider identity and demonstrates that the console/network facts came through the pinned CEF/native provider path. A separately labelled reference fixture remains useful but cannot satisfy the real-provider claim.
